Work Requested: Attend site to investigate and repair
Job Information: Recently I have been attending The Doug Larsen BMX park in Beenleigh of an afternoon.
Around 6pm the lighting comes on so the park can be used at night. Whilst there are many lights there 3 of
them are not working creating shadows across the park. To many this may not seem like a big issue but to
those using the park correctly it makes parts of the facilities unsafe for use.
Q Power attended Doug Larsen BMX Park to investigate multiple lights not operating. The lighting control was located in
the top right-hand side of the switchboard beside the BMX clubhouse.
On inspection, 4 lights were found operating. 2x of the 4x fittings operating drivers were identified as faulty intermittently
Pole 5 has 2 x out of service tags and 2 x failed drivers. Lights not operating.
Pole 8 has 1 x out of service tag on driver 2. Faulty driver, light half operating.
Pole 10, 11 and 12 have faulty drivers and are intermittently flashing on and off.
Pole 16 has an out of service tag by another contractor and is labelled with 2 x failed drivers. Light not operating.
PLEASE PAY BY        AMOUNT        INVOICE DATE

Please invesitgate The lights around the park at each of the benches have all stopped working, they stopped
one at a time. Now, it is dangerous to be walking around at night, especially because it is getting dark earlier.
The lights under each of the park benches roofs. Including the one in the dog park.
All the lights are on solar panels individually wired. None of them are connected to each other no a circuit breaker in a
switchboard. All segregated from each other.
Unplug light from panel, panel side connector testing 24 volts between negative and positive
No short between the panel negative and positive
Test button on the back of each light is not working, can’t get the light to start
Test the internal battery inside the lights, getting 11.3 volts. Unable to discern the battery specs as it’s an inbuilt
Solar lights are quite dusty so it’s possible it’s not producing enough charge although since there’s 24v I’m not sure
The battery voltage seems low even if the battery is a 12v, could be a faulty cell.
Lights also may be aging hence why they all went out individually.
As the solar panels are still functioning I believe that the lighting fixtures need to be replaced. Could not find any
markings on them to indicate what make or model they are.
Star - 8 Attended and installed new panel - Jess Notifed
